answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable token before it can post bids, with votes weighted by locked stake rather than account count. Splitting funds across a thousand identities does not multiply influence: each new identity dilutes the same stake, while tying it up prevents other uses. A ferrous supplier might whisper a low offer from a new account, but cannot gain extra weight without more capital; a ledge of slashed stake for provable fraud raises the cost further.
